message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** VM that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Create a project‑specific zone if you don’t have one yet
gcloud config set compute/zone us-central1-a   # choose your preferred zone

# 2. Create a new VM instance with:
#    • Standard machine type (e.g., n1-standard‑8)
#    • One RTX A6000 GPU
#    • Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image
#    • Preemptible option is optional – remove --preemptible if you want a regular instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \   # <-- replace with RTX A6000
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=50GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: add a startup script
```

> ⚠️ **Important:**  
> * Replace `nvidia-tesla-a100` with the correct accelerator type for RTX A6000. As of now, the official accelerator type for RTX A6000 is `nvidia-tesla-a6000`.  
> * Ensure you have enabled the **Compute Engine API** and the **NVIDIA GPU Driver** package installed on the instance (you can install drivers via the startup script).  

### Example startup script (`startup.sh`) to auto‑install NVIDIA drivers:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y linux-headers-$(uname -r) build-essential dkms
wget https://us.download.nvidia.com/XFree86/Linux-x86_64/535.54.03/NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-535.54.03.run
chmod +x NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-535.54.03.run
sudo ./NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-535.54.03.run --silent
```

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (HTTP POST)

If you prefer to use the raw REST endpoint, here’s a minimal JSON payload you can POST to the Compute Engine API:

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      },
      "autoDelete": true,
      "mode": "READ_WRITE"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  }
}
```

**Endpoint**

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json
Body: <above JSON>
```

Replace:

* `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` with your actual GCP project ID.
* `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN` with a valid OAuth 2.0 token that scopes `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.

---

### Quick checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Enable **Compute Engine API** in your project. |
| ✅ | Verify you have enough quota for GPUs in the selected zone. |
| ✅ | Install NVIDIA drivers after boot (via startup script or SSH). |
| ✅ | Attach a persistent disk if you need more than the default 50 GB. |

Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or region to match your workload requirements!
